title: Aphelion visual and weekly position log refinement
content:
Aphelion received a focused browsing refinement pass after the initial live/runtime setup. The goal was to keep the interface calmer and more image-forward while making the weekly image arrangement recoverable later.

What changed:

  • Cleaner public surface: the main Aphelion background is now #FAFAFA, and the blue hover-square/crosshair drawing was removed from the canvas so the grid no longer flashes a highlighted block behind the preview.
  • Fixed inspection preview: hover previews no longer chase the cursor. The preview now sits centered as a fixed 800px square, and the generated placeholder image has been removed so the card stays blank until the real thumbnail is available.
  • Cursor settled back: after testing an edge-aware diagonal arrow, the canvas cursor returned to the standard crosshair because it better fits the precision-grid interaction.
  • Weekly image constellation: Aphelion now randomizes server-loaded images deterministically by ISO year/week, giving the wall a fresh layout each week while keeping that week stable across reloads.
  • Recoverable position logs: the server now creates a weekly position document in E:\aphelion\weeklog, titled like 2026-32.json, recording each display position with the original image id, code, title, image URL, folder label, and tags.

This keeps Aphelion feeling minimal in the browser while adding a useful memory layer underneath: each week can become its own recoverable arrangement instead of a temporary shuffle.
